heard: a 200-foot asteroid flew past Earth before anyone saw it. Most people believe space telescopes track every city-killing rock near our planet. But on July 13, 2023, asteroid 2023 NT-1 swept past at one quarter of the distance to the moon. Approaching directly out of the sun's blinding glare, the rock stayed completely hidden. Two days after it passed, an Atlas Observatory telescope in South Africa finally spotted it. The Chelyabinsk meteor used this exact solar-blind spot in 2013, injuring roughly 1,500 people. To catch these blind spot hazards, the European Space Agency is developing the NEOMIR spacecraft to launch around 2030. Without satellites monitoring the sun, solar glare can still blind our early warning systems.
